name: 1N4007
description: The default 1A general-purpose rectifier. The 1N400x series differs only in reverse voltage: 1N4001 is 50V, 1N4007 is 1000V. Just use the 1N4007 for everything. Banded end is the cathode.

DO-41.notes: axial body; the painted band marks the cathode.

typical_application: Mains/transformer rectification, polarity protection, relay and solenoid flyback clamps, low-frequency power circuits. For high-frequency switching use a fast or Schottky diode instead.
gotchas: band = cathode; reversing it in a bridge or clamp is a common error
slow reverse recovery (~30us): unsuitable for switch-mode and RF; use UF400x or a Schottky there
the 1N400x suffix only changes reverse voltage; pinout and current are identical, so default to 1N4007
~1.1V forward drop at 1A wastes more than a Schottky in low-voltage supplies
